purpose: Bromocriptine is used to treat several conditions including Parkinson's disease, certain hormone problems caused by high prolactin levels (like unwanted breast milk or missed periods), and type 2 diabetes. It can also be used to treat acromegaly, a condition where the body makes too much growth hormone. Your doctor prescribed it to help manage one or more of these issues.
how_it_works: Bromocriptine works by mimicking a chemical in your brain called dopamine. By acting like dopamine, it can help control movement in Parkinson's disease, lower high prolactin hormone levels, and help your body manage blood sugar better in diabetes. Think of it as a key that fits into certain locks in your brain and body to help things work more normally.
common_side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, headache, dizziness, and feeling lightheaded — especially when you stand up quickly. Some people also experience tiredness, constipation, or stomach upset. These effects are often worse when you first start the medication and may improve over time.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have low blood pressure, liver problems, or a history of mental health conditions, as this medication can sometimes cause confusion or unusual behavior. Rarely, it can cause sudden sleepiness, so be careful with driving until you know how it affects you. Do not drink alcohol while taking this medication, and always take it with food to reduce stomach upset. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, as many drugs can interact with bromocriptine.
typical_dosing: Dosing depends on what condition is being treated. For most conditions, you start with a very low dose (usually 1.25 mg once or twice a day with food) and slowly increase it as directed by your doctor. For diabetes (Cycloset brand), it is typically taken once in the morning within 2 hours of waking up. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and never change your dose on your own.
